newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish PM says March budget deficit over $1 bln.
newsitem.headline: Turkish PM says March budget deficit over $1 bln.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said the budget, targeted to be balanced for 1997, gave a deficit of more than $1 billion in March, the state-controlled Anatolian news agency said.

"The budget gave a deficit of a little more than $1 billion in March," the agency quoted him saying late on Sunday night after meeting President Suleyman Demirel, without giving any other items of the budgetary aggregates.

Erbakan had earlier said the budget was balanced in the first two months of the year, but his comment was challanged by a visiting International Monteary Fund (IMF) team last month and opposition parties.

The IMF said the budget deficit in the first quarter was 415 trillion lira ($3.05 billion) and opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz said last week the deficit was 520 trillion in the four months of this year.
The budget deficit was 1,217 trillion for 1996.
Erbakan said the budgetary revenues were about $1.5 billion in the first quarter, against a target of about $9 billion. He did not say why the figure fell sharply from the target.
He said the March budget deficit was caused by the Turkish press, which he blamed for creating "artificial agendas and disrupting economic and political stability".
"But we will pull together in May and June and ensure economic stability to make up for the losses in March," he said.
"We will try to earn the treasury $6 billion in May and $4 billion in June," he said. He did not elaborate.
